name: Ross River Paddle
description:
🚣🏽‍♂️ Registration with the leader is essential - please see below for contact details.
🚣 Unfortunately we don’t have any hire craft for this paddle

PADDLE DETAILS
We’ll meet at Loam Island (boat ramp) this Saturday at 0700, put our boats in the water and make our way along the river.  Which direction we head will depend on the conditions and where everyone wants to go.  Upstream we will reach a rock bar and can't go any further.  Downstream we can go towards Vickers Bridge.  Either way we get to see the beautiful trees that fringe the river, waterbirds, kites, maybe an eagle.  We could even get glimpses of freshwater reptiles.   So dust off the cobwebs, put the roof racks back on the car and join me for a fun couple of hours.

WHAT TO BRING
Sunscreen & insect repellent. 
Hat.
Long sleeves can prevent sunburn. 
Drinking water.
Watercraft & Paddle (Kayak, ski, SUP or the like) that is water worthy. 
If you are not a confident swimmer bring and use a life vest.
Waterproofing for any valuables you do not wish to get wet. 
Camera (or phone).  
A couple of snacks to enjoy at the half way mark before we return. 
Waterproof shoes or shoes that can get wet if you don't want to go barefoot. 
Sense of humour. 

REGISTRATION AND INFO
Please contact Phil via club email tsvbush@hotmail.com

Visitors are more than welcome. This will be a social paced paddle. Visitor fee = $5.

All participants must be 18+ years.

name: River bike ride
description:
This Saturday morning we’re planning a bike ride rather than a walk. Our route will take us along the Cranbrook and Aitkenvale side of the river before crossing over at Aplin’s Weir and returning via Annandale and Douglas. Depending on the group and trail conditions, we may detour to Douglas Mountain Bike Reserve for a lap around one of the lower green trails (please don’t let this put you off coming - it’s optional and if you wait for us, it won’t be too long). We’ll end our ride with a drink at Mocha Mecca. 

GRADE: Easy. This will be a flat ride at a social pace. 
DISTANCE: approx 13-14km. If the group decides, we can extend the ride to cross at Bowen Rd which will add another 6km.

EQUIPMENT:
Bike in good condition with functioning brakes and handlebar ends 
Helmet (should meet Australian safety standards)
Repair kit (including spare tube)
A few $ if you’d like to join us for a drink
Water (at least 1L). There are water fountains along the route to replenish
Sun protection, personal first aid kit
Enclosed shoes 

MEETING:
7am at Riverview Tavern carpark (247/251 Riverside Boulevard, Douglas)

TO REGISTER OR MORE INFO:
Contact Katherine by messaging the club FB page or email tsvbush@hotmail.com

Visitors welcome - $5 fee
All participants must be 18+ years

name: Foxlees Lookout, Upper Gold Creek and Mt Leach (Mt Spec region)
description:
SUNDAY 14 February 2021

REGISTRATION WITH THE WALK LEADER IS ESSENTIAL. PLEASE READ THE INFORMATION BELOW.

RATED: Hard. 
Off-track walking involving rock hopping on slippery rocks, walking in creek and on banks, negotiating obstacles. Good balance, agility and fitness required.

DESCRIPTION
This is an explorative walk. We'll start on track from the dam, and walk on-track for about 3 hrs to Foxlees Lookout. Then we'll leave the track network, find the start of upper Gold Creek, and have an adventure down the creek to Gold Creek Falls before re-join the track network. The walk back to the dam will be 2hrs on-track. 
If we have two groups, then the fast group will go back to Mt Leach via the ridgeline, then 3 hrs on track back to the carpark.

WHAT TO BRING
- Water: min. 2L and refill from creek or 4L for the full day. **see below info.
- Clothing: full long sleeve and long pants are recommended. Many members also wear fingerless gloves.
- Enclosed footwear. Shoes that can get wet are appropriate eg runners. Leather is not a good option.
- Food for the day
- Hat, sunscreen and insect repellent
- Usual bushwalking gear 
- Personal first aid kit including a compression bandage and blister kit is recommended.

** Water: if you are uncomfortable using creek water for drinking water refill (after treating suitably), then carry 4L min for the day, or more to suit your requirements. Note that the club recommends that any natural water sources must be suitably treated before consumption.

COST
Non members = $5 walk fee for insurance
Must be over 18years to participate

WALK LEADER, INFO and REGISTRATION
Walk leader is Luen
To discuss suitability, to register or for more information please contact Luen on luenwarneke@gmail.com.

WALK DETAILS
Meet time: 0800 Paluma Village Green (cnr Mt Spec Rd and Smith Cres, adjacent to the Community Centre)
Return time: 5pm at Dam

name: Blue Gum Circuit (Paluma)
description:
SUNDAY 7 February 2021

Blue Gum Circuit: A great track walk on the Blue Gum Creek circuit. The club developed this track back in 2013. You'll see waterfall and creek scenery, rainforest and woodland, old tin mining areas and enjoy a lovely swim or two. There is a steep 400 mr elevation climb back to Paluma village though.

REGISTRATION WITH THE WALK LEADER IS ESSENTIAL. PLEASE READ THE INFORMATION BELOW.

RATED: hard (due to the elevation gain).

DESCRIPTION
This track walk starts in Paluma village before descending on the south side of Paluma into the Blue Gum / upper Star Valley area. There will be several steep descents. At the bottom, we'll walk and rockhop alongside creeks. There will be a couple of creeks that require crossing (one with boots off) and others that require rock hopping skills. Our efforts will be rewarded with a swim at the lagoon at lunch time - one of the great lagoons we visit.  
 
After lunch – the climb back to Paluma is a 3 hour 400m elevation climb up a steep bush track. We'll stop at Triple Falls on the way for another swim or to just enjoy the scenery.

FITNESS
If you can comfortably do Castle Hill four times up the goat track non-stop (with a day pack), then you should be fit enough for this climb.

WHAT TO BRING
- Water: min. 2L and refill from creek or 4L for the full day. **see below info.
- Clothing: full long sleeve and long pants (or long gaiters) are recommended as there is some off track walking that may include scratchy/sharp vegetation. Many members also wear fingerless gloves.
- Enclosed footwear
- Food for the day
- Hat, sunscreen and insect repellent
- Usual bushwalking gear 
- Personal first aid kit including a compression bandage and blister kit is recommended.
- Hiking poles (optional) can be useful on track and for creek crossings but can be cumbersome during off track walking (recommend that poles can be folded or collapsible to be stowed during these sections).

** Water: if you are uncomfortable using creek water for drinking water refill (after treating suitably), then carry 4L min for the day, or more to suit your requirements. Note that the club recommends that any natural water sources must be suitably treated before consumption.

COST
Non members = $5 walk fee for insurance
Must be over 18years to participate

To discuss suitability, to register or for more information please contact tsvbush@hotmail.com and we will get back to you asap.
